one_liner: Cloud accounting platform with extensive public APIs for financial data

evidence.claim: Xero uses OAuth 2.0 (authorization code and PKCE flows) as its documented authentication model; no plain API key auth
evidence.quote: OAuth 2.0 is a protocol that lets your app access a user’s account without accessing their password. Your app requests specific permission scopes and is granted an access token upon a user’s approval.

evidence.claim: API calls are made with a Bearer access token plus a tenant id
evidence.quote: you can make API calls by providing both a valid access token and authorized tenant id with each request

evidence.claim: Developers can self-serve: sign up for a free Xero account, use the demo company, and register an OAuth 2.0 app to get a Client ID/Secret
evidence.quote: Signup for a free Xero account; Enable the Xero demo company · Add your OAuth 2.0 application

evidence.claim: Broad REST API surface: Accounting API alone documents dozens of endpoints, plus Assets, Bank Feeds, Files, Finance, Payroll (AU/NZ/UK), Projects and more
evidence.quote: creating transactions like invoices and credit notes, right through to extracting accounting data via our reports endpoint

evidence.claim: Xero officially ships an MCP server (XeroAPI GitHub org, linked from its docs AI toolkit section)
evidence.quote: We've developed an MCP server that seamlessly integrates with Xero's public API, allowing LLMs to interact with business data

notes: Uncertified apps are limited to 25 tenant connections; exceeding that requires app certification/partner program. 'Custom Connections' (client_credentials, single org) carry a monthly fee (~$10 AUD) but standard OAuth flows are free. Some endpoints deprecated (Expense Claims, Receipts, Practice Manager 3.0). Access tokens expire in 30 minutes; refresh tokens last 60 days. Official MCP server at github.com/XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server.
